newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to Jan 17.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of January 17 were $8.10 billion, compared to $6.597 billion on January 10.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of January 17 were $17.710 billion, compared to $17.863 billion as of January 10.
It said the increase of $1.503 billion in net international assets during the same period was due to:
- The sale of $1.5 billion by the federal government to the Banco de Mexico, which was used by the central bank to pre-pay debt to the International Monetary Fund.
- Net deposits and currency sales by state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $174 million.
- Net sales of foreign currency to the federal government worth $107 million.

- A net loss of $64 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
The central bank said that between January 10 and 17, the monetary base rose by 363 million pesos 78.779 billion pesos.

The balance of the government's deposits at the central bank rose by 464 million pesos due to an increase in government spending of 11.266 billion pesos -- an increase that was covered in part by the sale of $1.5 billion by the federal government to the central bank as part of the IMF repayment.
The central bank offset the increase in liquidity from the higher government spending by increasing deposits by financial institutions in the central bank by 9.956 billion pesos.

*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
